summary: Members ask a seat's host how far its seats got with a message, on the seat-freshness relay (db break-up step 4b, the relay)

replay.detail: No claim, replication or replay changes. A read carries a host's local marks and stream lifecycle to the member that asked, which keeps the answer a few seconds in memory and stores nothing.

rules.detail: Lifecycle rules are unchanged. A message to a seat whose host keeps its receipts reads as the further of this member's own state and the host's answer; a host that does not answer reads as unknown, never as sent.

compatibility.detail: New member-authenticated route POST /v1/peer/seat-freshness/reads (worker-only daemon route /v1/internal/seat-freshness/reads), advertised by the new daemon.started feature seat_freshness_reads = 1. A member asks only a host that advertises it, so a release without it is never asked and is read from lifecycle claims as before; a worker that answers the route's unsigned 404/405 reads as unknown. Graph mail is asked about only when its host also advertises message_offsets, which no release writes yet, so until then only a stream item whose recipient is on another host is read through the relay: conversations status now shows how far that host took it instead of unknown. The doctor message-delivery, mail-backlog and held-mail checks and conversations cleanup read the same way once a host advertises message_offsets, and name any host that did not answer.

recovery.detail: Rolling back is safe: the previous release neither serves nor asks the route, and its peers stop asking it once its daemon.started without the feature replicates.
